$comment: Open-set verdict. This is the only definition of the rule: public/js/verdict.js (browser) and tools/verdict.py (pipeline) read it and hold no thresholds of their own. Signals: fit = mean over the scored answers of the cosine between each answer's standardized, nuisance-projected Hellinger feature and the winning model's centroid (bank.robust.hellinger), i.e. the absolute agreement the core discards when it standardizes across models; margin = that fit minus the best fit of any other model; p_family = summed probability of the winning model's family. Bank entries are grouped by bare model id first, so two channels of one model are one candidate. Rule, in order: fit < fit_min -> insufficient; margin >= margin_min -> match; p_family >= family_min -> family_only; else insufficient. 'observed' is the outcome table on the evidence in tools/reports/2026-09-13-open-set-verdict/records.jsonl, written by tools/verdict_fit.py --write-outcomes and re-checked by tools/tests/test_verdict.py.

messages.match: The answers fit one model in the bank clearly better than any other.
messages.family_only: The answers fit this family, but the models inside it are too close to name one.
messages.insufficient: The answers do not fit any model in the bank well enough to say. Run the challenge again, or the model may not be in the bank yet.

channel_note: The fingerprint tracks the model, not the channel it was collected through; the channel of the pasted answer is not determined.
